body.description: Returns true if input is a number (including infinity). It is a more reasonable alternative to `typeof n` which returns `number` for `NaN`.

example.text:
> t.isNumber(0)
true
> t.isNumber(1)
true
> t.isNumber(1.1)
true
> t.isNumber(0xff)
true
> t.isNumber(0644)
true
> t.isNumber(6.2e5)
true
> t.isNumber(NaN)
false
> t.isNumber(Infinity)
true

body.description: Returns true if input is a finite number. Identical to `isNumber` beside excluding infinity.

example.text:
> t.isFiniteNumber(0)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(1)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(1.1)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(0xff)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(0644)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(6.2e5)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(NaN)
false
> t.isFiniteNumber(Infinity)
false

body.description:
A plain object is a simple object literal that is not an instance of a class. Returns `true` if the input `typeof` is `object` and is not `null` plus either has a _direct_ prototype of `Object.prototype` or `null`.

@param {*} input - The input to test

example.text:
> t.isPlainObject({ something: 'one' }) // object literal
true
> t.isPlainObject(Object.create(null)) // null-prototype plain object
true
> t.isPlainObject(new Date())
false
> t.isPlainObject([ 0, 1 ])
false
> t.isPlainObject(/test/)
false
> t.isPlainObject(1)
false
> t.isPlainObject('one')
false
> t.isPlainObject(null)
false
> t.isPlainObject((function * () {})())
false
> t.isPlainObject(function * () {})
false

body.sig: * An array-like value has all the properties of an array yet is not an array instance. An example is the `arguments` object. Returns `true`` if the input value is an object, not `null`` and has a `length` property set with a numeric value.
* Returns true if the typeof input is `'object'` but not null.
* Returns true if the input value is defined.
* Returns true if the input value is undefined.
* Returns true if the input value is null.
* Returns true if the input value is not one of `undefined`, `null`, or `NaN`.
* Returns true if the input value is an ES2015 `class`.
* Returns true if the input is a string, number, symbol, boolean, null or undefined value.
* Returns true if the input is a Promise.

body.description:
* @param {*} input - The input to test
* @returns {boolean}
* @static
* @example
* > t.isIterable('string')
* true
* > t.isIterable(new Map())
* true
* > t.isIterable([])
* true
* > t.isIterable((function * () {})())
* true
* > t.isIterable(Promise.resolve())
* false
* > t.isIterable(Promise)
* false
* > t.isIterable(true)
* false
* > t.isIterable({})
* false
* > t.isIterable(0)
* false
* > t.isIterable(1.1)
* false
* > t.isIterable(NaN)
* false
* > t.isIterable(Infinity)
* false
* > t.isIterable(function () {})
* false
* > t.isIterable(Date)
* false
* > t.isIterable()
* false
* > t.isIterable({ then: function () {} })
* false
body.sig: * Returns true if the input is an iterable (`Map`, `Set`, `Array`, Generator etc.).
* Returns true if the input value is a string. The equivalent of `typeof input === 'string'` for use in funcitonal contexts.
* Returns true if the input value is a function. The equivalent of `typeof input === 'function'` for use in funcitonal contexts.

body.description:
* @param {*} input - The input to test
* @returns {boolean}
* @static
* @example
* > t.isAsyncFunction(function () {})
* false
* > t.isAsyncFunction(new Function())
* false
* > t.isAsyncFunction(() => {})
* false
* > t.isAsyncFunction(async function () {})
* true
* > const AsyncFunction = async function () {}.constructor
* > t.isAsyncFunction(new AsyncFunction())
* true
* > t.isAsyncFunction(async () => {})
* true
* > class Command { async execute () {} }
* > t.isAsyncFunction(new Command().execute)
* true
body.sig: * Returns true if the input value is an async function or method.
